site.name: Moony
site.tagline: Your whole net worth. Only on your computer.
site.description: Moony is a free, open-source personal finance app for macOS, Windows and Linux. Bank accounts, investments, crypto, property, loans and insurance in one encrypted database on your own computer. No account, no cloud, no telemetry.

footer.blurb: A personal wealth manager that stays on your computer.
footer.disclaimer: Moony is not financial, tax or investment advice. Figures depend on data from third parties and may be inaccurate.
footer.nocookies: This site sets no cookies and loads nothing from third parties.

modules.title: A balance sheet, not just a budget.
modules.intro: Most apps track spending or investments. Moony holds both sides of your finances in one place, so the number at the top is the real one.

bank.name: Bank accounts
bank.what: Import statements as CSV, keep the full transaction history, search and filter.

budgets.name: Budgets
budgets.what: Limits per category with progress, rules that categorize new transactions for you.

cashflow.name: Cashflow
cashflow.what: Where money came from and went, plus a planning view for the months ahead.

stocks.name: Stocks and ETFs
stocks.what: Positions with cost basis, time-weighted and money-weighted return, a watchlist with target prices.

crypto.name: Crypto
crypto.what: Prices from CoinGecko, transaction log, share of the portfolio.

assets.name: Real estate, bonds, other assets
assets.what: Dated valuations, rental income and costs, linked loans and policies, bond coupons, documents.

loans.name: Loans
loans.what: Balance as of a date, extra payments and rate changes re-anchor the schedule.

insurance.name: Insurance
insurance.what: Premiums, frequency, payment calendar, attached documents.

tools.name: Projection and analysis
tools.what: Where you may land in a chosen number of years from your returns and monthly contributions, stock analysis per tag, two calculators.

modules.foot: Figures are shown in the main currency you choose: any of 36 currencies with ECB reference rates; accounts and holdings can use 45.

ledger.title: The complete list. Written to be checked against the code.
ledger.intro: Moony makes network requests only for the things below. Apart from the optional AI client you connect yourself, none of them involves your balances, amounts, names or documents.

yahoo.sent: Ticker symbols of the stocks you hold or follow, search text you type, symbols and ISINs from a stock CSV you import, and date ranges for price history.
yahoo.when: After unlock, when you add or import stock transactions, open the stock monitor or a position, and when prices are stale.

coingecko.sent: The CoinGecko IDs of your crypto holdings, search text, and date ranges for history. If you add your own API key, it goes in a request header.
coingecko.when: After unlock, when you add a holding and when history is back-filled.

ecb.sent: Nothing about you. A download of the public daily reference rates.

frankfurter.sent: The date range from your oldest transaction to today and the currencies your transactions use, to fetch historical ECB rates.
frankfurter.when: When you add or import transactions in a currency whose history is missing, and on rate refresh.

github.sent: A plain request for latest.json of the latest release. The updater adds its user agent: app name and version, operating system and CPU architecture. An update you accept is checked against the project's public key.
github.when: Once per app start, after unlock.

ai.sent: Whatever your AI client asks for over a local port, potentially your full financial data. Moony itself sends nothing to an AI provider.
ai.when: Only while the MCP server is enabled, the app is unlocked and a client connects with your token.

data.label: Your balances, transactions, names, documents
data.value: Moony never sends them to any service.

ledger.foot: The web view that renders the interface loads nothing from the internet. All requests go through the Rust backend.
ledger.encrypted: The database: every record you enter or import, AES-256 with SQLCipher. The key is protected by your password and a 24-character recovery key. There is no backdoor.
ledger.plain: Photos and documents you attach are stored as plain files in the data folder, also inside backup archives, and the JSON export is plain text. Full-disk encryption is the right complement. Encrypting attachments is on the roadmap.
